# Incident Report: PCAP Forensic Analysis — 2022-01-07 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Evidence Reviewed
Only one artifact was present in the evidence directory: `2022-01-07-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,880 frames, 4.6 MB). No IDS/Suricata alert export or other artifacts were provided, so attribution below is **behavioral**, not signature-confirmed.

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **192.168.1.216** | Sole local host driving all suspicious traffic; heaviest conversation in `conv,ip` |
| MAC | **9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==192.168.1.216`) and Ethernet source on all frames from .216 |
| Hostname | **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** | DHCP option 12 hostname bound to MAC `9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9`; confirmed by Kerberos client principal `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic. (NBNS broadcasts a near-identical variant `DESKTOP-GXNYNO2` — DHCP/Kerberos are the more reliable sources per methodology.) |
| Logged-in user | **steve.smith** | Kerberos `CNameString` on AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 192.168.1.216 and the domain controller 192.168.1.2 |

Domain: `spoonwatch.net` (AD domain controller `SPOONWATCH-DC` at 192.168.1.2). LAN gateway: 192.168.1.1 (MAC `1c:17:d3:f6:df:0a`).

## Malware Family
**Vidar Stealer** (or a Vidar-family info-stealer variant) — **behavioral attribution**, not signature-confirmed (no IDS export was supplied with this evidence).

Basis for attribution:
- **Bare-IP C2**, no DNS lookup preceding it: a single persistent HTTP/1.1 keep-alive TCP session (stream 65, port 49738→80) to `2.56.57.108` starting cold at t=202.9s with no domain resolution, download, or lure activity visible anywhere earlier in the capture.
- **No `User-Agent` header**; `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8` on every request — consistent with Russian-market crimeware-as-a-service tooling.
- Seven sequential `POST /osk//N.jpg` requests (N=1–7) each return HTTP 200 with `Content-Type: image/jpeg`, but the actual downloaded bytes are **PE32 DLLs / legitimate third-party runtime libraries** (confirmed via `file`/`strings`): `sqlite3.dll` (via a mingw/libgcj runtime), `MSVCP140.dll`, `VCRUNTIME140.dll`, `CONCRT140.dll`, `CRYPT32.dll`, `WSOCK32.dll`, `WINMM.dll`. This is Vidar's well-known technique of fetching legitimate helper DLLs disguised as `.jpg` to read and decrypt Chromium/Firefox SQLite profile databases (cookies, autofill, saved logins) rather than shipping its own SQLite/crypto code.
- `POST /osk//main.php` — check-in/config request.
- `POST /osk/` uploads a 379,629-byte multipart body named `_5861695120.zip` whose internal directory structure is a classic stealer log layout, organized **by data category then by browser**:
  - `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`
  - `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt` (credit-card autofill)
  - `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt`, `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt`

No delivery chain (initial infection vector) is observable in this capture — traffic before t=203s is normal AD domain-join/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB authentication with the DC (192.168.1.2) plus Windows telemetry and Windows Update; nothing resolves or downloads an initial dropper. The stealer's execution predates or falls outside this capture window.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` — HTTP, sole C2 session, evidence: TCP stream 65, frames 1498–4830

**URLs**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` — module/DLL downloads (frames 1501, 1641, 2225, 2541, 2691, 3054, 4194)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` — check-in (frame 4275)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` — exfil upload endpoint (frame 4816)

**Transferred files (downloaded to victim, disguised as .jpg)**
| Requested name | True type | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| 1.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` |
| 2.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` |
| 3.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` |
| 4.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` |
| 5.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` |
| 6.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` |
| 7.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` |

**Exfiltrated file (uploaded from victim to C2)**
- `_5861695120.zip` (379,629 bytes), stolen browser data (autofill, saved credit-card autofill, cookies for Chrome and Edge). SHA256 of the POST body as captured: `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f`

## Benign Context (not IOCs)
- Windows Update / Delivery Optimization traffic: `download.windowsupdate.com`, `au.download.windowsupdate.com`, `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` (IPs 23.38.189.225, 23.38.189.201, 8.253.189.126) — legitimate `.cab` definition updates and a signed Defender delta patch.
- Microsoft telemetry/services: `self.events.data.microsoft.com`, `v10/v20.events.data.microsoft.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`, `pti.store.microsoft.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`, `dns.msftncsi.com`, `api.msn.com`, `www.bing.com`.
- Active Directory domain traffic to `192.168.1.2` (SPOONWATCH-DC): LDAP/CLDAP, Kerberos, SMB/SMB2, DCE-RPC (drsuapi, netlogon, lsarpc, samr) — normal domain-joined workstation behavior for user `steve.smith`.
- ARP, NBNS, mDNS, LLMNR, SSDP, IGMP broadcast/multicast noise.

## Incident Summary
Windows workstation `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2` (192.168.1.216, MAC `9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9`), logged in as domain user `steve.smith` on the `spoonwatch.net` AD domain, was compromised by an information stealer consistent with Vidar (behavioral attribution). The malware beaconed to bare-IP C2 `2.56.57.108:80`, pulled down legitimate helper DLLs (SQLite, VC++ runtime, WinSock) disguised as sequential `.jpg` files to parse Chrome/Edge browser data, checked in via `main.php`, and exfiltrated a 379 KB ZIP of stolen autofill, credit-card-autofill, and cookie data for Chrome and Edge to `/osk/`. No delivery chain is visible in this capture; the malware was already resident and began its C2/exfil cycle at t=202.9s.
